svg.text: How jevisualeyes composes a preset — code enumerates, the model picks one, code renders. Every choice has a receipt.
Provider: local decision model (Laya) · Jev optional · fixture in every test

g.text: Place the tag on the axes
The app asks the model to set one coordinate per stack
from the tag phrase and the record's knob descriptors.
"slow organic, cool palette" · record: gyroid (surface + lighting +
symmetry + raymarch stacks, 23 knobs, measured bounds)
Model chooses (all axes in ONE request — independent given the tag):
motion slow · density medium · contrast soft · palette cool
No genre names anywhere: a style is a point on these axes.
Ladders are ORDINAL situations, never numbers — code maps them.
In the same request, one yes/no per candidate parameter:
"should this move under this tag?" — a probability each.
0.5 means "unsure", not "a little". The band is calibrated on
labelled looks, per provider — a Jev threshold does not transfer.
Why the same request: the axes and the motion flags are
independent given the tag, so they ride one call and cannot
see each other. A hop exists only where the next MENU is
No model call. For each stack the sampler draws N coherent,
complete looks from the coordinate, seeded.
Every candidate is valid by construction
full parameter vector inside every knob's [MIN, MAX] · ops from
the shared roster · layer state · FX chain · stable id · one-line
readable description. Out-of-bound looks are never generated.
Candidates for the SURFACE stack (3 of 8):
lighting (8) · symmetry (6) · raymarch/shade ops (8) · layers (4) · FX (6)
The menu bounds what can exist. If a look is not on any menu,
no tag can produce it — the model picks the closest thing.
Rosters are READ from the app's canon at run time, never copied.
One Choice per stack over its sampled looks — all
stacks in one request. A real hop: these menus did
model choice = the argmax · varied = seeded sampling over the
Strict validation first: keys == candidates, finite, sum ≈ 1,
chosen == argmax. Anything else is an ERROR, never a random pick.
A wrong pick is still on the menu; it can never invent a knob.
Only a TRAINED provider's probabilities are confidence.
A logit-reading LLM may serve the argmax, never a band.
Only if stage 2 marked anything as moving. Per moving parameter,
one waveform Choice over the real modulator roster and one rate
Score over ordered situations — all in one request.
Resulting binds (code turns the ladder into a value)
surface.fold ← LFO sine, rate level 1 → 0.08 Hz, bracket inside the knob's range
lighting.keyAngle ← LFO triangle, rate level 1 → 0.05 Hz
raymarch.palette.shift ← LFO sine, rate level 0 → 0.02 Hz
Binds ride the app's data router like any other source. A Score is
ordinal — "1.2" is not 20% of the way to "pulses"; it is thresholded.
The model never does arithmetic, never orders dates, never writes a
value. Ordinal → number is code (rate table per record family).
On the 2-slot ONNX export this stage waits for the reference runtime
(Score + N-way Choice are the conversion's limit, not the model's).
No model call. The runner builds one card snapshot per tag,
attaches the 2–3 receipts as provenance and saves it as a
named slot through the app's own preset path — never a
params { surface: S_r5_med …, lighting: L_k3 …, symmetry: Y_2f …, raymarch: R_p1 … }
generation.provenance [ receipt CALL1, receipt CALL2, receipt CALL3 ]
Each receipt: request hash · candidate-map version · prompt-template version · provider id
· model id · full distribution · chosen id · selection policy · usage · latency.
Any knob in the preset traces to the question it answered, the menu
it saw, and the option that won — or to a manual edit, labelled as such.
The preset walk carries all of it: values, brackets, binds, ops, layers.
A choice that does not survive a recall is a bug, not a feature gap.
Provider id + model id + question roster + template version + thresholds
are ONE versioned unit. Same stored receipts + same seed replay exactly;
a live rerun does not — and says so.
Repeat per tag · regenerate what is unlocked
The bake runs stages 1–6 for every (record, tag). Later edits
regenerate only the unlocked stacks; locked ones are hard context.
Edits that never call the model
set a value · pick a blend · lock/unlock · duplicate · rename — deterministic,
"keep the surface, calm the lighting" → ONE Choice over a fixed operation
set {regenerate, lock, set-axis, unsupported, ambiguous} + target stack.
Resolves to a lock + a regenerate — never a whole-preset rewrite.
What the loop guarantees, and what it does not
Code guarantees: bounded menus, valid values, no protected edits, finite
jobs, one durable commit per decision, parseable presets, full receipts.
It cannot guarantee taste. The model cannot see the render. A valid
all-default look fails the eye; the user (or a later vision judge) says so,
and the runner offers another variation — never a hidden fallback.
Cost: 2–3 calls per (record, tag). Bake of 495 records ≈ 5,000 calls —
under a dollar on Jev, zero on the local provider.
Fixture provider = deterministic synthetic decisions; every test and gate
runs on it with zero network. Live smoke is one call behind an explicit flag.
